BLOCKER: Acceptance criterion 3 unmet: tests cover only `_normalize_paths`; no test exercises `_changed_modules`/scoped detection or the `--all` escape hatch (missing-test blocker per standards).

`_git_changed` now silently strips `product-forge/` for *all* consumers; diff does not show `_changed_modules`/`_changed_files`, so it is unverified that every caller expects normalized paths — any caller comparing against repo-relative paths will silently under-scope checks (integrity risk).
MAJOR: `merge-base origin/develop HEAD` silently falls back to `"HEAD"` when the remote ref is absent/stale, and the blanket `except Exception: return []` hides failures — a stale or missing ref yields zero changed files, skipping module checks with no observability.

Porcelain rename handling is fragile: `ln[3:]` + `" -> "` split mishandles quoted paths (`"go/a b.go" -> "go/c d.go"`) and filenames containing ` -> `; correct side must be parsed and unquoted individually.

Diff output lines are not stripped of the `product-forge/` prefix consistency check before status merge is deduplicated — no dedup at all; the same file from diff+status produces duplicate entries, inflating module scoping lists.
MINOR: `--all` parsed via `"--all" in sys.argv[1:]` bypasses any arg validation; undocumented in usage/help, and `--all` combined with other flags has no guard.
`_normalize_paths` returns a flat list with duplicates and no ordering guarantee; consumers doing membership tests are fine but any set/count logic would be wrong.
`git status --porcelain` unmerged (`UU`, `AA`) states are treated as normal paths; conflict states should probably be surfaced rather than silently scoped.
NIT: Test asserts membership only; no negative assertions (e.g., non-`go/` paths excluded, no duplicates, backslash normalization).
Test imports a private `_normalize_paths` directly; a public helper or contract-level test would survive refactors better.
SUMMARY: Solid direction: porcelain normalization and `--all` escape hatch address real scoping gaps, and the normalization is extracted testably. Top risks: the required scoped-detection test is missing, the `product-forge/` strip silently rewrites the `_git_changed` contract for unseen consumers, and silent `origin/develop`→`HEAD` fallback can mask under-scoped CI runs with no logging.
